candidates.decision_relevance: Would align BTC and ETH price paths with short-horizon returns and other observations, helping distinguish persistent deterioration from a brief rebound and assess event order.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily analyses repeatedly report unavailable or undersized nominal hourly windows and mismatches between nominal and actual observation spans. Existing 168-hour ETH/BTC persistence does not provide the corresponding BTC and ETH price paths.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped BTC and ETH hourly close series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Without continuous, cutoff-aligned hourly observations, the analyses cannot reliably reconstruct short-horizon moves or determine whether weakening observations preceded or followed price changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether participation changes persist across a stable constituent set rather than reflecting proxy snapshots or changing membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily and weekly analyses repeatedly describe breadth as proxy-only, point-in-time, and affected by differing membership; no comparable historical constituent-level sequence is supplied.
candidates.metric_name: Constituent-level daily returns and membership for the breadth universe
candidates.missing_history_problem: Changing-universe snapshots prevent testing whether breadth genuinely broadened or deteriorated over time, and limit comparison with price and leadership paths.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify whether the cited positive or mixed settled flow observations persisted, reversed, or were concentrated in particular sessions relative to market deterioration.
candidates.evidence_reference: The supplied analyses repeatedly characterize ETF evidence as one settled session or report that the settled sequence is unavailable; they do not provide a continuous dated flow history.
candidates.metric_name: Dated settled BTC and ETH ETF net flows
candidates.missing_history_problem: Isolated settled totals cannot establish the direction, persistence, or timing of flows relative to price and breadth changes.
